epc.name: En Primeur Club, Tuscany vintage report (archive of Decanter and critic notes)

claims.claim: Winter and spring were cool, which delayed the vine cycle in both Chianti Classico and Bolgheri. May was cool and wet inland. Bolgheri had a cold, rainy April and May, with budbreak over ten days late.
Flowering inland came in mid-June, warm and dry, and went quickly with little shatter.
Hail hit parts of Chianti Classico. Badia a Coltibuono lost yield to July hail.

Summer was moderate inland, with no repeat of the 2017 heat and drought. Late August rain prevented water stress. Bolgheri had a very hot, dry June and drought until late July, then cooler weather. The consortium describes sunny, stable weather to the end of harvest.
claims.note: Zones differ in June; sources agree on a stable late season.

claims.claim: September had good weather and big day and night temperature swings, which helped phenolic ripeness.
Harvest inland ran from late September through most of October. Bolgheri ran from 5 September to early October.
Chianti Classico produced about 275,000 hl, roughly 10% above average. Jancis Robinson reportedly notes Tuscany made about 10% more wine than in 2018.
claims.note: The critic article is read. The Robinson point is from a search summary. Bolgheri yield not stated.

claims.claim: Chianti Classico: fresh, crisp acidity, ripe phenolics, slightly lower alcohol and vivid colour, with cool-night acidity credited for the best wines. Vinous reportedly found the 2019s mid-weight and somewhat uneven.
claims.note: Critics split on consistency. Vinous view from a search summary only.

claims.claim: Bolgheri: five stars from Decanter. Ripe black cherry, dark plum, graphite and herbs, with velvety tannins and a saline finish. Top wines may last 25 years or more. The consortium calls it outstanding.
claims.quote: outstanding from all points of view

conflicts: Chianti Classico consistency: the Consorzio and Italy's Finest Wines give five stars, but Vinous reportedly calls the wines mid-weight and uneven. The Consorzio says yields were high and the Circle article says tannins in some wines were not fully ripe.
gaps: Florence hills and Valdarno not covered separately.
Vinous and Decanter 2019 articles not read in full.

sheet.vintage: 2019 started cool and late, then settled into a steady summer with cool nights. Chianti Classico is fresh and bright, and Bolgheri is ripe and polished.
